stem: A platform team calls a module straight from GitHub with `source = "github.com/acme/queue-module"`. A colleague merged an unfinished change into the repository's primary branch, and the next fresh workspace picked it up during initialization. The team wants every new workspace to receive the code of the release tagged v2.3.0. What should they change?

choices.text: Add a `version = "2.3.0"` argument to the module block
Rewrite the address as `git::https://github.com/acme/queue-module.git` with nothing else changed

rationale: The `ref` query parameter accepts a tag name, so naming the release tag fixes which revision is cloned. The `version` argument applies only to registry modules, so it does not select a revision of a GitHub repository. A branch name is accepted by `ref` as well, but a branch keeps moving as commits arrive, so it does not fix a version. The explicit `git::` form of the same repository still follows the default branch at HEAD when no `ref` is given.
